Performers
Jascha Brodsky (violin I), Charles Jaffe (violin II), Max Aronoff (viola), Orlando Cole (cello) Documented

The Internet Archive description credits the Curtis String Quartet with these four players and assigns Brodsky to violin I and Jaffe to violin II. The label of side 1 (MM-405 pressing, 70344-D) names Brodsky and Jaffe as violins, Aronoff as viola and Cole as cello, without assigning the violin parts.

[1] [6]
Work version
The complete quartet, four movements on seven sides Inferred, not documented

The item lists the movements and parts side by side; the edition used by the players is not identified.

[1]
Recorded
1940-03-06 Documented

The Internet Archive description gives 6 March 1940. No second source for the date was found.

[1]
Place
New York City Documented

The studio is not named.

[1]
Label
Columbia Masterworks Documented

Issued as a 78-rpm album set.

[1] [6] [5]
Catalogue
M-405 (69849-D to 69852-D); automatic sequence AM-405 (69853-D to 69856-D); later reissue MM-405 (70344-D to 70347-D) Documented

The label scanned in the item reads MM 405-1, 70344-D, the drop-automatic reissue pressing. The item description says the set was issued in May 1940; Columbia’s October 1940 catalogue lists all three number ranges.

[1] [6] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Sides 1–⁠7, matrices XCO 27013 to 27019; side 8, XCO 27020, is Tchaikovsky’s scherzo and is not part of this recording Documented

Side 1: first movement, part 1; side 2: first movement, part 2; side 3: second movement, part 1; side 4: second movement, part 2 and third movement, part 1; side 5: third movement, part 2; side 6: third movement, part 3 and finale, part 1; side 7: finale, part 2. Take numbers are not given.

[1]
Transfer
Shellackophile collection, Internet Archive Documented

No personal mastering credit is given.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was added to the Internet Archive on 4 July 2022; the date of the transfer is not stated.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Equipment, equalisation and restoration are not stated. The file is a single continuous MP3 of the seven sides.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Smetana died on 12 May 1884; the composition is in the public domain. Documented

The death date is from the Bedřich Smetana Museum. This does not cover a later edition or arrangement.

[4]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: first issued in 1940, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule applies to a Columbia set issued in 1940: the former 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 2011 extension applied on 1 November 2013. The Internet Archive description gives the issue as May 1940. Columbia’s own October 1940 catalogue independently lists the set as M-405 (69849-D to 69852-D), so the first issue was no later than October 1940. This is not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.
